newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Aerolineas Argentinas unable to sell routes.
newsitem.headline: Aerolineas Argentinas unable to sell routes.

text.p: Spain's government, the largest shareholder in Argentina's Aerolineas Argentinas, will be unable to sell or transfer routes assigned to the airline, saidthe daily Clarin Thursday.
"The routes belong to the state and therefore Iberia can negotiate various things apart from selling or stopping of services on routes," an Argentine government source told Clarin.
The statements come after recent speculation that Aerolineas is about to enter into an alliance with American Airlines which could involve route swaps or sales.
Spain is currently seeking new strategic alliances to strengthen the commercial base of Iberia and the other airlines in which it has interests such as Aerolineas and Venezuelan airline Viasa.

On Wednesday Spain's Industry and Energy Minister Josep Pique said Spain will "continue to be involved in the operation, the management and the personality of the company (Aerolineas)," and that there were no plans to sell.
The Spanish government owns around 45 percent of Aerolineas through a direct 20 percent stake held by state-owned Iberia Lineas Aereas de Espana SA and another stake in a holding company.
